Ben / Kim —

Thanks for the summary. A few clarifications from procurement/legal side: Fortuna will need the invoice cadence documented in the order form (section: Payment Schedule) and the invoices split to mirror the three pricing bands so our accounting team can match to POs.

On withholding: Fortuna is required by our tax team to withhold taxes on vendor services when applicable. We prefer Redwood not to require a gross-up (we can provide official withholding certificates), but if Redwood’s policy requires gross-up for liability reasons we need to see that in writing.

Net terms: our standard is Net-60; however, the finance team may accept Net-45 for strategic partners. For the pilot phase we can accept quarterly billing but we need payment timing explicitly in the order form and the invoice recipient entity mapped.

Please send updated redline and sample invoice template.

Regards,
Asha Patel
Head of Procurement, Fortuna Health

Forwarding our redline and tax analysis — please see attached PDF (Fortuna_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf) and a short tax summary spreadsheet. Key notes in the redline:

- Payment schedule (Section 2.1): proposed quarterly invoicing in arrears tied to usage band thresholds; line items break out activation fee and usage credits.
- Net terms (Section 2.3): standard Net-45 in master, with a negotiated Net-60 exception clause for Fortuna's Class B entity documented as a one-time exception tied to the first two invoices; Finance to re-evaluate after month 6.

- Invoicing recipient (Appendix A): added explicit entity mapping rows to ensure POs align with invoices.

1) Net terms: Redwood can commit to the one-time Net-60 concession for the first two invoices for Fortuna's Class B entity as requested. We will include a short clause that the concession is tied to on-time submission of POs and withholding documentation.
